sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/MID MO VALLEY/CNTRL PLAINS
sections.text: AN UPPER-LEVEL TROUGH WILL PROGRESS EWD INTO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS TODAY AS A WELL-FOCUSED LOW-LEVEL JET MOVES NNEWD FROM THE CNTRL PLAINS THIS MORNING INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST THIS AFTERNOON. ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS PERHAPS WITH A HAIL THREAT SHOULD BE ONGOING ON THE NOSE OF THE LOW-LEVEL JET IN ND AND NRN MN THIS MORNING. AT THE SFC...A LOW WILL MOVE NEWD ACROSS SD AROUND MIDDAY WITH THE MOIST AXIS EXTENDING SWD FROM THE LOW ACROSS THE MID MO VALLEY AND EWD ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY WHERE SFC DEWPOINTS ARE FORECAST TO BE IN THE MID TO UPPER 60S F. THIS SHOULD YIELD MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY ACROSS A BROAD WARM SECTOR BY AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE VALUES FORECAST TO BE IN THE 2000 TO 3500 J/KG RANGE. IN ADDITION TO THE INSTABILITY...A 65 TO 80 KT MID-LEVEL JET IS FORECAST TO EJECT NEWD ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS WHICH WILL CREATE MODERATE DEEP LAYER SHEAR PROFILES FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS. MODEL FORECASTS SUGGEST THAT SFC-BASED THUNDERSTORMS WILL FIRST INITIATE IN CNTRL MN JUST NORTHEAST OF THE SFC LOW DURING THE MID AFTERNOON WITH STORMS EXPANDING IN COVERAGE SWWD INTO FAR SE SD AND NE NEB BY EARLY EVENING. THE THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL SHOULD BE GREATEST EARLY IN THE EVENT WHEN CELLS HAVE

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY TO CENTRAL PLAINS THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: OVERNIGHT CONVECTION HAS EVOLVED INTO AN MCS ACROSS CENTRAL/NE WI AS OF 12Z...AND OUTFLOW WITH THIS CONVECTION REINFORCED A STALLED SURFACE FRONT ACROSS SRN MN/CENTRAL WI. THIS BOUNDARY WILL MOVE NWD TODAY AS THE MORNING STORMS EXIT WI...AND A SURFACE LOW DEVELOPS NEWD FROM S CENTRAL SD TO W CENTRAL MN THIS EVENING...IN ADVANCE OF A MIDLEVEL TROUGH MOVING EWD FROM MT/WY TO THE DAKOTAS. A CORRIDOR OF 68-70 F BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IS PRESENT ALONG AND S OF THE BOUNDARY...AND THE MOISTURE WILL BE MAINTAINED BENEATH A WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER SPREADING NEWD FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS. THE COMBINATION OF AFTERNOON TEMPERATURES WARMING INTO THE 80S/LOWER 90S AND THE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WILL SUPPORT STRONG WARM SECTOR INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON FROM NE NEB/ERN SD ACROSS MN/WI. ADDITIONALLY...DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR...AND LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL BE MAXIMIZED ALONG THE WARM FRONT FROM CENTRAL MN TO NRN WI. THE PRIMARY CONCERN TODAY WILL BE THE TIMING AND DISTRIBUTION OF STORMS...GIVEN THE WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AND ASSOCIATED CAP. SINCE SURFACE TEMPERATURES ARE NOT LIKELY TO WARM ENOUGH TO REMOVE CONVECTIVE INHIBITION IN THE OPEN WAR

sections.title: CENTRAL PA/NY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: THE LOW LEVELS WILL GRADUALLY DESTABILIZE FROM W-E IN THE WAKE OF MORNING WAA CLOUDS/CONVECTION ACROSS PA/NY. THOUGH MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL NOT BE STEEP...THE INCREASE IN LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AND DAYTIME HEATING WILL SUPPORT MODERATE SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY...COMBINED WITH 25-30 KT EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR...WILL SUPPORT A RISK FOR ISOLATED STRONG/DAMAGING GUSTS. ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 06/19/2012

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER NORTHEAST LOWER MI
sections.text: AN AMPLIFYING UPPER TROUGH IS PRESENT THIS MORNING OVER THE NORTHWEST U.S...WHILE UPPER RIDGING MAINTAINS CONTROL OVER THE REMAINDER OF THE NATION. AT THE SURFACE...A LOW IS ANALYZED OVER CENTRAL SD WITH A PRONOUNCED WARM FRONT EXTENDING EASTWARD INTO SOUTHERN MN. THIS LOW AND WARM FRONT ARE FORECAST TO MOVE NORTHWARD THROUGH THE DAY...ALLOWING A VERY MOIST/UNSTABLE AIR MASS TO SPREAD ACROSS MUCH OF SOUTHERN/CENTRAL MN. THIS WILL SET THE STAGE FOR A ROUND OF STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT SCATTERED ELEVATED CONVECTION WILL PERSIST THROUGH MUCH OF THE DAY ACROSS CENTRAL/NORTHERN MN WHERE WARM ADVECTION AND LIFT IS OCCURRING. A FEW OF THESE STORMS COULD PRODUCE MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL. THE PRIMARY SEVERE CONCERN WILL EVOLVE LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING AS STORMS DEVELOP ALONG THE SURFACE WARM FRONT OVER CENTRAL MN AND NORTHEAST SD. A COMBINATION OF MLCAPE VALUES OVER 3000 J/KG AND STRONG LOW LEVEL/DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL PROMOTE SUPERCELL/BOW STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND A FEW TORNADOES. THIS ACTIVITY MAY CONGEAL INTO A FAST-MOVING BOW ECHO DURING THE EVENING...TRACKING ALONG THE CORRIDOR OF HIG

sections.title: SD/NEB
sections.text: FARTHER SOUTHWEST...THE LOW LEVEL JET IS FORECAST TO BECOME VERY STRONG OVER NEB AFTER DARK. THIS SHOULD HELP TO INITIATE SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ALONG AND JUST BEHIND THE SURFACE COLD FRONT MOVING ACROSS THE AREA. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW AMPLE CAPE AND SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR FOR A RISK OF HAIL-PRODUCING STORMS.

sections.title: UPPER MI
sections.text: A LONG-LIVED BOW ECHO CONTINUES TO TRACK EASTWARD ACROSS UPPER MI. LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS REMAIN POSSIBLE ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF THE STORMS. THE ACTIVITY SHOULD MOVE INTO LAKE HURON AFTER 18Z...ENDING THE SEVERE THREAT ACROSS THIS REGION. ..HART/MOSIER.. 06/19/2012

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: CONSIDERED AN UPGRADE TO A WIND-DRIVEN MODERATE RISK IN PARTS OF CNTRL MN. A STRONGLY UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR IS PREVALENT S OF A WARM FRONT ARCING ACROSS E-CNTRL SD TO NRN WI WITH PRIMARY SURFACE LOW NEAR HON AND AHEAD OF A COLD FRONT EXTENDING SWWD INTO SWRN NEB. VERY STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR EXISTS WITHIN THE WARM FRONTAL ZONE. PRIMARY CONCERN IS WITH REGARD TO WARM MID-LEVEL TEMPERATURES AS LEAD SHORT WAVE IMPULSE IS WELL REMOVED TO THE NW ALONG THE MT/SASKATCHEWAN BORDER...AND UPSTREAM IMPULSE IS STILL OVER THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN WEST. CONVERGENCE INVOF SURFACE LOW SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR TSTM DEVELOPMENT BY EARLY EVENING...BEYOND THE ELEVATED ONGOING CONVECTION OVER NRN MN. UPSCALE GROWTH AND CONSOLIDATING COLD POOLS WILL BE NECESSARY FOR AN MCS TO OVERCOME OPEN WARM SECTOR INHIBITION. IF THIS INDEED OCCURS...POTENTIAL IS CERTAINLY THERE FOR HIGHER-END COVERAGE/INTENSITY OF ALL SEVERE TYPES.

sections.title: CNTRL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: WITH APPROACH OF THE SHORT WAVE IMPULSE OVER THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN WEST...ASCENT WILL STRENGTHEN AND YIELD TSTM CLUSTERS AFTER DARK. SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR AND MUCAPE WILL EXIST FOR HAIL-PRODUCING STORMS AND THUS HAVE EXTENDED SLIGHT RISK WWD. ..GRAMS.. 06/19/2012 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1110 AM CDT TUE JUN 19 2012/ AN AMPLIFYING UPPER TROUGH IS PRESENT THIS MORNING OVER THE NORTHWEST U.S...WHILE UPPER RIDGING MAINTAINS CONTROL OVER THE REMAINDER OF THE NATION. AT THE SURFACE...A LOW IS ANALYZED OVER CENTRAL SD WITH A PRONOUNCED WARM FRONT EXTENDING EASTWARD INTO SOUTHERN MN. THIS LOW AND WARM FRONT ARE FORECAST TO MOVE NORTHWARD THROUGH THE DAY...ALLOWING A VERY MOIST/UNSTABLE AIR MASS TO SPREAD ACROSS MUCH OF SOUTHERN/CENTRAL MN. THIS WILL SET THE STAGE FOR A ROUND OF STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT SCATTERED ELEVATED CONVECTION WILL PERSIST THROUGH MUCH OF THE DAY ACROSS CENTRAL/NORTHERN MN WHERE WARM ADVECTION AND LIFT IS OCCURRING. A FEW OF THESE STORMS COULD PRODUCE MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL. THE PRIMARY SEVERE CONCERN WILL EVOLVE LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING AS STORMS DEVELOP ALONG THE SURFACE WARM FRONT OVER CENTRA

sections.title: SD/NEB
sections.text: FARTHER SOUTHWEST...THE LOW LEVEL JET IS FORECAST TO BECOME VERY STRONG OVER NEB AFTER DARK. THIS SHOULD HELP TO INITIATE SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ALONG AND JUST BEHIND THE SURFACE COLD FRONT MOVING ACROSS THE AREA. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW AMPLE CAPE AND SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR FOR A RISK OF HAIL-PRODUCING STORMS.

sections.title: UPPER MI
sections.text: A LONG-LIVED BOW ECHO CONTINUES TO TRACK EASTWARD ACROSS UPPER MI. LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS REMAIN POSSIBLE ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF THE STORMS. THE ACTIVITY SHOULD MOVE INTO LAKE HURON AFTER 18Z...ENDING THE SEVERE THREAT ACROSS THIS REGION.

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY/NRN PLAINS
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY CURRENTLY SHOWS SWLY FLOW IN PLACE ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS AND UPPER MS VALLEY WITH AN MCS GOING IN NCNTRL MN. THE STORMS ARE MOSTLY ELEVATED BY SHOULD POSE A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. FURTHER TO THE SOUTH...THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A WELL-DEFINED WARM FRONT EXTENDING FROM A 998 MB SFC LOW IN ERN SD NEWD ACROSS CNTRL MN. ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY...A POTENT ENVIRONMENT IS IN PLACE WITH MLCAPE VALUES ESTIMATED IN THE 2000 TO 3000 J/KG...0-6 KM SHEAR OF 40 TO 50 KT AND 0-1 KM SHEAR OF 20 TO 30 KT. THIS WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS AND TORNADOES IF CELLS CAN INITIATE ALONG THE BOUNDARY EARLY THIS EVENING. AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR STRONG TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY SUPERCELL THAT CAN BECOME SFC-BASED AND MOVE NEWD PARALLEL TO THE BOUNDARY WHERE LOW-LEVEL SHEAR IS ENHANCED. A LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE THREAT SHOULD EXIST WITH SUPERCELLS. A WIND DAMAGE THREAT SHOULD EXIST WITH BOWING LINE SEGMENTS. AT THIS POINT...MODEL GUIDANCE CONTINUES TO INITIATE SFC-BASED THUNDERSTORMS FROM ERN SD NEWD INTO CNTRL MN WHERE THE ENVIRONMENT IS VERY FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS. THE ONLY QUESTION IS TIMING AND COVERAGE AND SO FAR CONVECTION HAS NOT DEVE

sections.title: SRN SD/NCNTRL NEB
sections.text: ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS FORMED BREIFLY IN NCNTRL NEB ALONG A SLOW-MOVING COLD FRONT. THE AIRMASS IS CHARACTERIZED WITH MODERATE INSTABILITY WITH MLCAPE OF 2000 TO 2500 J/KG AND 40 TO 50 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR. IN SPITE OF THE FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR SEVERE STORMS...FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST A WEAK CAPPING INVERSION IS PRESENT WHICH MAY KEEP THE STORMS STRUGGLING OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. LATER THIS EVENING...CONVECTIVE COVERAGE IS EXPECTED TO MARKEDLY INCREASE AS A 50 TO 60 KT LOW-LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS ACROSS THE CNTRL PLAINS. BY 06Z...NUMEROUS ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO DEVELOP NORTH OF THE BOUNDARY ACROSS SRN SD AND NRN NEB. FORECAST SOUNDINGS IN THIS AREA AT 06Z SHOW THE GREATEST INSTABILITY SOUTH OF THE SD STATE-LINE WITH MUCAPE AROUND 1500 J/KG. THIS COMBINED WITH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND 40 KT OF EFFECTIVE SHEAR SHOULD BE ENOUGH FOR A LARGE HAIL THREAT WITH THE MORE INTENSE CELLS. ..BROYLES.. 06/20/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS EXPECTED TO PERSIST ACROSS WW 410...ATTENDANT TO TWO LINES OF STORMS MOVING EWD ACROSS NERN WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 1240Z...REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED TWO LINES OF STORMS IN NERN WI /LEAD BAND EXTENDS FROM MARINETTE-WAUPACA COUNTIES WI...AND SECOND LINE EXTENDING FROM LANGLADE TO NRN PORTAGE COUNTIES WI/. THE LEAD ACTIVITY WAS MOVING EWD AT 40-45 KT WHILE THE SECOND BAND CONTINUED WITH ITS 50 KT MOVEMENT. ALTHOUGH THE 12Z GRB SOUNDING SUGGESTED THIS ACTIVITY MAY BE ROOTED JUST ABOVE THE SURFACE...DCAPE AROUND 1000 J/KG WOULD SUPPORT A THREAT FOR STRONG WINDS AS THIS ACTIVITY PROGRESSES EWD THROUGH MID MORNING. ..PETERS.. 06/19/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: NEW WW MAY BE NEEDED ACROSS NRN LOWER MI AS BOWING LINE OF STORMS SHIFTS EWD INTO THIS REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST OBJECTIVE ANALYSES AND MORNING APX /ALPENA MI/ RAOB REVEAL A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIRMASS ABOVE A SHALLOW STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER. MORNING HEATING CONTINUES TO REDUCE STABILITY IN THIS SHALLOW SURFACE-BASED LAYER HOWEVER...WITH TEMPERATURES NOW IN THE MID TO UPPER 70S. THUS -- WITH A BOW ECHO MOVING EWD IN EXCESS OF 40 KT NOW EXITING NRN WI AND MOVING INTO NRN LK MI...THREAT FOR LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS MAY INCREASE E OF THE LAKE /ACROSS NRN LOWER MI/ OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE THREAT STEADILY ENDING FROM W TO E ACROSS THE WW AREA AS THE BOWING STORM CLUSTER SHIFTS TOWARD/INTO LK HURON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS THE BOWING STORM CLUSTER SHIFTING QUICKLY EWD ACROSS NERN LOWER MI AND INTO NRN LK HURON ATTM...WITH JUST A FEW LAKESHORE COUNTIES IN NERN LOWER MI WHERE LIMITED/ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND THREAT PERSISTS. AS STORMS CONTINUE SHIFTING OFFSHORE OVER THE NEXT HALF HOUR TO HOUR...SEVERE THREAT WILL GRADUALLY COME TO AN END ACROSS THIS AREA. ..GOSS.. 06/19/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT WILL CONTINUE FROM THE TX GULF COAST NWD INTO CNTRL/N-CNTRL TX. ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS AS WELL AS HEAVY RAIN ARE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS. ISOLATED/LOW SEVERE THREAT IS ANTICIPATED AND SHOULD PRECLUDE THE NEED FOR A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED IN THE WARM...MOIST...AND UNSTABLE AIR MASS ACROSS SE/CNTRL TX. THIS AIR MASS IS CHARACTERIZED BY A WARM/MOIST PROFILE THROUGH A LARGE PART OF THE TROPOSPHERE...EVIDENCED BY PWATS GREATER THAN 1.75 INCHES ON 16Z DERIVED SATELLITE IMAGERY AND SKINNY MLCAPE PROFILES /NORMALIZED CAPE BELOW 0.15 PER THE LATEST MESOANALYSIS/. MLCAPE VALUES AROUND 1000-1500 J/KG COMBINED WITH THE MODERATELY STRONG LOW-LEVEL FLOW /0-1 KM BULK ABOVE 15 KTS/ AND STORM MOTION ABOVE 25 KTS WITH SUPPORT GUSTY WINDS IN A FEW STORMS. OVERALL SEVERE THREAT APPEARS LOW BUT SOME THUNDERSTORM WIND DAMAGE MAY OCCUR. ADDITIONALLY...AFOREMENTIONED MOIST PROFILE WILL SUPPORT HIGH RAIN RATES WITH RAINFALL TOTALS GREATER THAN AN INCH POSSIBLE DESPITE THE QUICK STORM MOTION. ISOLATED/LOW SEVERE THREAT SHOULD PRECLUDE THE NEED FOR A WW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED WITHIN THE NEXT HR OR TWO OVER PORTIONS OF WRN/N-CNTRL NEB. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 2130Z...A COLD FRONT EXTENDED SWWD OUT OF ERN SD AND ACROSS N-CNTRL INTO WRN NEB. OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS GUIDANCE SHOWS VERY STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES HAVE DEVELOPED ALONG THE FRONT...WHICH IS AIDING IN STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION. THIS DESTABILIZATION COMBINED WITH CONVERGENCE AND ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT IS RESULTING IN DEEPENING CUMULUS...WHICH MAY EVOLVE INTO ISOLATED/SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS DURING THE NEXT HR OR TWO. LATER IN THE NIGHT...STORM COVERAGE MAY INCREASE FURTHER ALONG/BEHIND THE FRONT AS ASCENT INCREASES WITH APPROACHING UPPER TROUGH. IN THE MEANT TIME...LATE AFTERNOON SURFACE CONDITIONS CHARACTERIZED BY TEMPERATURES FROM 90-100F...DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S TO LOW 60S...AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE YIELDING MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY. THOUGH STRONGEST VERTICAL WIND SHEAR RESIDES OVER THE COOL SIDE OF THE COLD FRONT...A FEW SVR STORMS POSING A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE THROUGH THE EVENING GIVEN THE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMICS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: UNCERTAINTY LINGERS CONCERNING TIMING OF BOUNDARY LAYER BASED WARM SECTOR DEVELOPMENT...AND INITIATION OF MORE VIGOROUS CONVECTION WITHIN LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION TO THE NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT. HOWEVER...ONE OR MORE WATCHES LIKELY WILL BE NEEDED BY EARLY EVENING...PERHAPS WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VERY WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR CONTINUES TO PROVIDE STRONG INHIBITION TO CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT...BOTH IN THE WARM SECTOR OF THE DEEP EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA CYCLONE...AND WITHIN AT LEAST A NARROW CORRIDOR TO THE NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT EXTENDING TO THE EAST NORTHEAST...ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL MINNESOTA. THE VERY MOIST WARM SECTOR HAS BECOME MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE BENEATH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...WITH MIXED LAYER CAPE NOW ON THE ORDER OF 2000-3000+ J/KG. AND DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS STRONG AND FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS...WITH LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS SIZABLE AND SUPPORTIVE OF TORNADIC POTENTIAL...MAINLY ALONG THE WARM FRONT. LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE APPEARS MAXIMIZED NEAR THE SURFACE LOW...FROM HURON INTO THE WATERTOWN AREA...AND DEEPENING CONVECTION IS ALREADY EVIDENT TO THE NORTH OF HURON. GUIDANCE IS ALSO SUGGESTIVE THAT A WEAKNESS IN THE INHIBITION MAY EXIST ACROSS THIS VICINITY...SOUTHWARD ALONG A PRE-FRONTAL SURFACE TROUGH INTO NORTHEAST NEBRASKA...ALONG WHICH SHALLOWER CUMULUS DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN EVIDENT. MEANWHILE...AN INCREASE IN STORM DEVELOPMENT DOES APPEAR UNDERWAY TO THE NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT...ACROSS PARTS OF SOUTHEASTERN NORTH DAKOTA INTO WEST CENTRAL MINNESOTA...WHICH THE LATEST HIGH RESOLUTION RAPID REFRESH SUGGESTS MAY EXPAND CONSIDERABLY AND GROW UPSCALE THROUGH THE 00-02Z TIME FRAME. WHILE THE EVOLUTION OF CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS REMAINS A BIT UNCLEAR...THE GREATEST SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL...INCLUDING THE RISK FOR TORNADOES...APPEARS TO EXIST WITH CONVECTION NEAR THE HURON/WATERTOWN AREAS...IF AND WHEN THE CAP FINALLY BREAKS LATE THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO INITIATE AND SPREAD EWD OUT OF FAR ERN WY/NEB PANHANDLE/SWRN SD INTO PORTIONS OF WRN NEB AND S-CNTRL SD TONIGHT. THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL WILL ACCOMPANY THIS ACTIVITY. AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WV IMAGERY AT 0130Z SHOWS AN UPPER-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING E ACROSS THE NRN GREAT BASIN. IN RESPONSE TO THIS DISTURBANCE...LOW-LEVEL WINDS OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS ARE BECOMING MORE ELY...WHICH WILL AID IN WWD ADVECTION OF MOISTURE TOWARD THE EDGE OF THE EML. THIS MOISTENING COMBINED WITH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES /REFER TO 00Z LBF RAOB/ IS FORECAST TO RESULT IN INCREASING MUCAPE VALUES /RANGING FROM 1000-2000 J PER KG/ ROOTED NEAR 700 MB. AS LOW TO MIDLEVEL FRONTOGENESIS STRENGTHENS AHEAD OF THE UPR TROUGH...BANDS OF ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS SHOULD DEVELOP ACROSS THE AREA. STRONG MIDLEVEL SWLYS SPREADING ACROSS THE REGION WILL CONTRIBUTE TO EFFECTIVE BULK WIND DIFFERENCE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 50 KT...WHICH WILL FAVOR ROTATING STORMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A WW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE RISK FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS MAY BECOME THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREATS...BUT SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT WITH TORNADO POTENTIAL STILL CANNOT BE RULED OUT THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA SURFACE LOW CENTER HAS BEGUN TO WEAKEN. MODELS INDICATE THAT THIS FEATURE MAY MIGRATE NORTHEASTWARD ALONG THE FRONTAL ZONE INTO WEST CENTRAL MINNESOTA DURING THE 03-05Z TIME FRAME. BUT THE SOUTHWESTERLY 850 MB JET IS STILL EXPECTED TO STRENGTHEN FROM 40-50+ KT...INCREASING LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR AND ALONG THE WARM FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS SOUTHEASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA NORTHWARD THROUGH CENTRAL MINNESOTA. THE PRIMARY LIMITING FACTOR CONCERNING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AND SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL REMAINS THE STRONG CAPPING BENEATH VERY WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR. AS THE WARM SECTOR BOUNDARY LAYER BEGINS TO SLOWLY COOL...HIGHEST PROBABILITIES FOR NEW CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT SEEM TO REMAIN IN A CORRIDOR OF STRONGER FORCING ABOVE/NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT...IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO INFLOW OF AIR EMANATING FROM THE MOIST WARM SECTOR BOUNDARY LAYER CHARACTERIZED BY SURFACE DEW POINTS NEAR 70F. ..KERR.. 06/20/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG TO ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS POSING A THREAT FOR GUSTY WINDS AND HAIL ARE LIKELY TO PERSIST ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL AND NORTHEAST MN FOR A FEW MORE HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: BANDS OF DEEP CONVECTION CONTINUE TO SPREAD GENERALLY ENEWD ACROSS CNTRL AND NCNTRL MN TO THE NORTH OF A DISTINCT WEST-TO-EAST WARM FRONT SITUATED OVER SCNTRL MN. WARM/MOIST AIR BEING LIFTED ISENTROPICALLY ACROSS THIS FRONTAL ZONE SHOULD CONTINUE TO FUEL A FEW MORE VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS...PRIMARILY ALONG THE SRN EDGE OF THE WATCH AREA...ESPECIALLY ACROSS CROW WING AND AITKIN COUNTIES IN THE SHORT-TERM WHERE IR IMAGERY DEPICTS CLOUD TOPS CONTINUE TO COOL AND LIGHTNING FLASH RATES HAVE ALSO RECENTLY INCREASED. MUCH OF THE AIR MASS ACROSS NERN MN HAS LIKELY BEEN OVERTURNED FROM REPEAT CONVECTION AND SEVERE POTENTIAL IN THIS PORTION OF THE WATCH HAS LIKELY ENDED. HOWEVER...FARTHER WEST...NEW UPDRAFT DEVELOPMENT HAS RECENTLY SHOWN UP ON RADAR AND SATELLITE DATA ACROSS EXTREME ERN/SERN ND...PERHAPS IN RESPONSE TO INCREASED LIFT ACROSS THE WARM FRONT WITH THE ONSET OF THE NOCTURNAL LOW LEVEL JET AND/OR APPROACH OF WEAK MID LEVEL HEIGHT FALLS. ..CARBIN.. 06/20/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CURRENT TRENDS SUGGEST THAT BOTH THE REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF TORNADO WATCH 413 AND SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 412 MAY BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE AS CURRENTLY SCHEDULED AT 06Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SOME RECENT INTENSIFICATION OF CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT HAS OCCURRED WEST THROUGH NORTH OF ALEXANDRIA DURING THE PAST HOUR OR SO... WHERE A STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL JET IS MAINTAINING MOISTURE RETURN ABOVE/NORTH OF THE QUASI-STATIONARY FRONTAL ZONE. A NARROWING PLUME OF STEEPER MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES PERSISTS ACROSS PARTS OF EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA INTO WEST CENTRAL MINNESOTA...CONTRIBUTING TO INSTABILITY. HOWEVER...WEST SOUTHWESTERLY MEAN FLOW WILL SUPPORT CONTINUED EASTWARD ADVECTION OF THIS ACTIVITY INTO AN ENVIRONMENT STABILIZED BY PERSISTENT CONVECTION ACROSS NORTH CENTRAL AND NORTHEASTERN MINNESOTA INTO THE LAKE SUPERIOR REGION. LITTLE IS NOW EVIDENT TO SUGGEST SUBSTANTIVE FURTHER INTENSIFICATION OF CONVECTION...AND ACTIVITY MAY TEND TO FINALLY SHIFT EASTWARD OUT OF MINNESOTA INTO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION BY THE 07-08Z TIME FRAME...WHILE UPSTREAM CONVECTION REMAINS SLOW TO DEVELOP NORTHEASTWARD OUT OF THE DAKOTAS. ..KERR.. 06/20/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE NEED FOR A WATCH IS NOT CERTAIN...BUT TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR AN INCREASING SEVERE THREAT THAT COULD REQUIRE A WATCH WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MOISTURE WITHIN A NORTHEASTERLY POST-FRONTAL LOW-LEVEL FLOW ACROSS CENTRAL/WESTERN SOUTH DAKOTA INTO WESTERN NEBRASKA REMAINS SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT AT LEAST WEAK CAPE...BENEATH STEEP LAPSE RATES ALOFT. AND THIS APPEARS LIKELY TO MAINTAIN A DEVELOPING CLUSTER OF STORMS SPREADING NORTHEASTWARD WITH MID/UPPER FORCING OUT OF SOUTHEASTERN WYOMING. DEEP LAYER SHEAR...ASSOCIATED WITH VEERING OF MODERATE NORTHEASTERLY NEAR SURFACE FLOW TO 30-40 KT OUT OF THE SOUTHWEST AT 500 MB...IS VERY STRONG...AND COUPLED WITH SIZABLE SUB-CLOUD TEMPERATURE/DEW POINT SPREADS...AN ORGANIZED STRONG WIND EVENT COULD CONTINUE TO EVOLVE THROUGH THE 06-09Z TIME FRAME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ALTHOUGH AN ISOLATED STRONG WIND GUST CANNOT BE RULED OUT AS A CORRIDOR OF STORMS CONTINUE TO MOVE NEWD THROUGH NORTH CENTRAL NEB...SRN-NERN SD INTO CENTRAL AND NERN MN...OVERALL DIMINISHING TREND IN INTENSITIES WILL PERSIST REDUCING THE SVR THREAT. GIVEN THAT THIS ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE TO TRAIN NEWD WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT WHERE PW VALUES ARE 1.5-1.9 INCH...HEAVY RAINFALL RATES WILL REMAIN A CONCERN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 08Z...SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWED A BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM SWRN NEB TO SERN SD INTO CENTRAL MN TO FAR NWRN WI /S OF DLH/. MEANWHILE...THE ONGOING ELEVATED TSTMS WERE DISPLACED 25-40 MILES N OF THE SURFACE BOUNDARY. THE OVERALL REDUCTION IN STORM INTENSITIES APPEARS TO BE TIED TO 1/ WEAKENING OF THE THERMODYNAMIC PROFILE /GREATER STABILITY CREATED THROUGH EXTENSIVE CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING/ AND 2/ DIMINISHING LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE AS THE LLJ VEERS. GIVEN THESE TRENDS...WW 415 HAS BEEN CANCELLED EARLY AND WW 416 WILL LIKELY BE CANCELLED EARLY AS WELL. ..PETERS.. 06/20/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A CORRIDOR OVER CENTRAL-EAST CENTRAL MN...EXTENDING 20 MILES EITHER SIDE OF A LINE FROM 35 E AXN TO 15 SW DLH...IS EXPECTED TO HAVE TRAINING STORMS PRODUCING MAINLY HEAVY RAINFALL RATES OF 1-2 INCH PER HOUR. THIS THREAT IS FORECAST TO PERSIST ON THE ERN EXTENT OF THE DISCUSSION AREA THROUGH 13-14Z. SOME HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER...SUSTAINED CELLS...BUT THE OVERALL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT DOES NOT WARRANT A SVR TSTM WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TRENDS IN SATELLITE IMAGERY AND SURFACE ANALYSES INDICATED A FRONTAL WAVE WAS DEVELOPING OVER WEST CENTRAL MN /INVOF ERN LAC QUI PARLE COUNTY/ AS FORCING FOR ASCENT SPREADS ENEWD ATTENDANT TO A PROGRESSIVE MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER SD. A GREATER EWD ADVANCEMENT WAS OCCURRING WITH THE ONGOING STORMS IN ERN SD...WHILE A FRONTAL ZONE IN CENTRAL MN TO NWRN WI AND WRN UPPER MI REMAINED NEARLY STATIONARY. REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY AND 7 KM AND 9 KM CAPPI INDICATED AN INCREASE IN STORM INTENSITIES WITH ACTIVITY ENE OF THE SURFACE LOW...WHILE ADDITIONAL STORMS WERE RAPIDLY FORMING NEWD TO SRN AITKIN COUNTY. THE NRN PART OF THE DISCUSSION AREA EXPERIENCED HEAVY RAINFALL TUESDAY EVENING INTO THE EARLIER OVERNIGHT PERIOD WITH VALUES RANGING FROM 3-6 INCHES. ADDITIONAL RAINFALL RATES OF 1-2 INCH PER HOUR WILL ONLY ACT TO EXACERBATE THE SITUATION WITH NEW RAINFALL BEING MAINLY RUNOFF. ..PETERS.. 06/20/2012
